interpretation: The raw Möbius combination separates two approximation obligations. Divisor cancellation gives the correct limit for every fixed basis coordinate, namely the coordinates of -E1, while convergence in the Hilbert norm would additionally require square-summable control uniform over coordinates that move with n. Relative to the triangular construction, its endpoint corrections enforce exact cancellation on a growing low-coordinate block; removing them preserves fixed-p convergence but leaves that block, as well as the intermediate coordinates, inside the unresolved domination range. Neither construction is thereby shown to have global l2 control.
source_support: Proposition 5 takes the coefficients mu(q)/q. The displayed divisor-sum rearrangement together with Lemmas 2 and 4 yields y_(n,1) -> -1 and y_(n,p) -> 0 for each fixed p > 1. The estimate <e_q,E_p> = O(q/p) gives y_(n,p) = O(n/p), from which the source states a p-only remote majorant for p >= n^2 log n. The extracted comparison glyph in that last majorant is damaged, so its exact typography is not reused.
nonparaphrase_operation: Decomposes coordinate targeting from norm convergence and identifies exact growing-block cancellation, rather than global energy control, as the specific service supplied by the omitted endpoint corrections.
speculation_status: The description in terms of mass migrating through n-dependent coordinates is an interpretation of why fixed-coordinate limits are insufficient, not a theorem that this span proves. No claim is made that the missing domination fails or that the remote majorant alone closes the approximation.
quality_reason: Accepted after replacing the candidate's overstatement about global energy control with the critic's bounded distinction between exact low-block cancellation and still-unproved global l2 domination; the readable formulas support the remaining claims despite one damaged comparison sign.

interpretation: Exponent smoothing creates a two-scale approximation: positive epsilon_n makes the omitted Möbius tails controllable by absolute estimates, while epsilon_n -> 0 moves the smoothed Dirichlet-series identities back toward the boundary target -E1. Under the stated sufficient lower bound epsilon_n >= 2 log log n/log n, this tradeoff preserves the fixed-coordinate limits and the O(n/p) remote decay. It does not supply the common l2 majorant on the remaining coordinates, and the span makes no necessity or optimality claim for that smoothing window.
source_support: Proposition 7 weights e_q by mu(q)/q^(1+epsilon_n), assuming epsilon_n >= 2 log log n/log n and epsilon_n = o(1). Its divisor-sum calculation invokes reciprocal-zeta identities and bounds both q > n tails directly; the displayed estimates tend to zero and give y_(n,1)(epsilon_n) -> -1 and y_(n,p)(epsilon_n) -> 0 for fixed p > 1. The proposition then extends the O(n/p) estimate and states the remote majorant beyond n^2 log n. The epsilon glyph and some comparison typography are extraction-damaged, so only the clearly recoverable assumptions and conclusions are retained.
nonparaphrase_operation: Reads the construction as balancing truncation control against return to a boundary exponent, and separates a sufficient rate condition from any unsupported claim of sharpness while exposing the still-open norm-convergence burden.
speculation_status: Calling this an Abel-type approach is only a conceptual analogy to approaching a boundary through a smoothed parameter; it is not source terminology or an optimality result. The source does not show here that smoothing unconditionally removes the natural scheme's low-coordinate obstruction.
quality_reason: Accepted after changing 'just enough' to an explicitly sufficient, non-sharp condition and preserving the critic's distinction between fixed-coordinate and remote-tail control versus the missing common l2 domination; OCR risk is confined to exact glyph typography.
